summary: The Gemara establishes that the incense must be placed on the coals inside the Holy of Holies (refuting the Sadducee position), the cloud of incense must fill the space before the High Priest approaches the ark, and the 'no man in the Tent of Meeting' exclusion applies only during the incense burning - not during blood sprinkling.

display.whats: Must the incense be lit inside the Holy of Holies, and how complete must the cloud be before the High Priest approaches the ark?
display.hint: The Sages derive from 'before God' that the incense must be placed inside - the Sadducees wanted to prepare it outside first. The cloud requirement is absolute: if it does not fill the space, the rite is incomplete. The 'no man' prohibition applies only during burning.
display.title: Inside the Cloud: Where Incense Atones

learning.ahaMoment: The incense rite embodies a theological principle: even the High Priest cannot approach the divine presence without mediation. The smoke cloud is not protection from danger - it is the act of reverence itself.
learning.memoryAnchor: The cloud of incense must fill the entire space of the Holy of Holies before the High Priest approaches the ark - the rite cannot be rushed.
learning.learnerQuestion: Must the incense be lit inside the Holy of Holies, and how complete must the cloud be before the High Priest approaches the ark?
learning.coreTension: The Sadducees held the incense should be lit outside so the High Priest enters already wrapped in smoke, while the verse 'before God' must be reconciled with the 'no man' exclusion and with how complete the cloud must be before any approach to the ark.
learning.coreMove: The Gemara reads 'before God' as requiring the incense to be placed on the coals inside the Kodesh Kodashim itself, reads 'so the cloud covers' as requiring the fill to be complete before approach, and limits the 'no man' exclusion to the duration of the burning itself.

takeaway.text: The incense must be placed on the coals inside the Holy of Holies, not prepared outside; the cloud must fill the space completely before the High Priest approaches the ark; the 'no man' exclusion applies only during the burning, not throughout the whole service.

learning.learningBlocker: Learners may assume the 'no man' prohibition excludes everyone from the Tent of Meeting for the entire Yom Kippur Holy of Holies service, missing that it applies specifically during the incense burning.

glossary.en: The gold cover of the Ark of the Covenant, with two cherubim on top; the cloud of incense covered this on Yom Kippur.
The incense offering burned on Yom Kippur inside the Holy of Holies; placed on coals, its cloud covered the ark.
Evil speech, slander; according to the Gemara, incense atones for this sin specifically.

rashiTranslations.en: Rashi: opens - [the High Priest] does this [the wearing of the eight garments] daily - [the Mishna explains this requirement].
Rashi: continues - [except] on Yom Kippur [when he wears four garments only] - [the eight garments are worn] on the [other] days [of the year].
Rashi: continues - [and all the people] in the [outer] courtyard - [they] were standing [when he performed the service].
Rashi: continues - [listening intently to hear the sound of the golden bells on his garment] - [so they would] know [that he had] come out [safely] from the Holy of Holies.
Rashi: continues - [the Mishna states:] and [he performed the] incense [service] - [this is the most important part of] the Day of Atonement service.
Rashi: continues - [the High Priest entered into the Holy of Holies] alone - [no other priest could be present during this act].
Rashi: continues - [and he brought] the incense pan - [filled with burning coals and incense].
Rashi: continues - [the High Priest] said: 'may it be [Your will] that this year be [a year of] mercy' - [he uttered this prayer].
Rashi: continues - [and he came] out - [from the Holy of Holies] after completing the incense service.
Rashi: continues - [the Mishna states:] and [he performed the] drawing [of the lots] on Yom Kippur - [two goats were brought].
Rashi: continues - [one [goat] for the Lord [to be sacrificed as a sin offering] and one for Azazel [to be sent to the wilderness] - [this] was written in the [Torah].
Rashi: continues - [the High Priest] cast [the] lots [between the two goats] - [to determine which would be for the Lord and which for Azazel].
Rashi: continues - [when] one [of the lots] came up [saying] 'for the Lord' - [this goat] was set aside [for sacrifice].
Rashi: continues - [and the other lot reading] 'for Azazel' - [this goat] was set aside [to be sent to the wilderness].
Rashi: continues - [the Mishna describes:] and [after the lots are drawn, the people rejoiced] - [because the] Azazel [goat] served [as a symbol of the sin being sent away].
Rashi: continues - [when the two goats were brought before him on Yom Kippur] - [the High Priest] laid [his] hands [upon them to perform the confession].
Rashi: continues - [the High Priest confessed over the goat designated for Azazel:] 'we have sinned' - [he recited the confession of sins].
Rashi: continues - [and confessed] all the [transgressions of the people of] Israel - [by listing their sins in categories].
Rashi: continues - [he laid] his hands [on the goat] and [the goat was taken away] to the wilderness - [thus the sin was symbolically removed].
Rashi: continues - [the Mishna continues:] and [the High Priest also] sacrificed the other goat - [the one whose lot said 'for the Lord'].
Rashi: continues - [this goat] was a sin offering - [it] atoned [for the sins of Israel].
Rashi: continues - [after all the rites were performed on Yom Kippur] - [the High Priest removed] his garments [and immersed in a mikvah].
Rashi: continues - [and then] he entered [the Holy of Holies] again - [to retrieve the pan and censer after the people had left].
Rashi: continues - [the Mishna states:] on all the other [days of the year the High Priest performs different rites] - [not like the service on Yom Kippur].
Rashi: continues - [the High Priest wears] eight [garments daily] - [this is the requirement for regular priestly service].
Rashi: continues - [but on Yom Kippur he wears only] four [garments] - [as specified for that holy day].
Rashi: continues - [the four garments are:] the tunic [ketonet], the breeches [michnasayim], the turban [mitznefet], and the sash [avnet] - [these are sufficient for the Day of Atonement].

Rashi: continues - [the other four garments worn on regular days are] the breastplate [hoshen], the ephod [efod], the robe [me'il], and the forehead plate [tzitz] - [these are not worn on Yom Kippur].
Rashi: continues - [the High Priest's service on Yom Kippur includes] entering [the Holy of Holies] once - [on the regular days he does not enter].
Rashi: continues - [but on Yom Kippur he enters] twice - [once with the blood of the goat for the Lord, once with the blood of the bull].
Rashi: continues - [each time he enters the Holy of Holies] he [must] recite the divine name [explicitly] - [this is done only on Yom Kippur].
Rashi: continues - [and] the people [are required to] fast - [on Yom Kippur all Jews must abstain from food and drink].
Rashi: continues - [and] all forbidden labors [are prohibited] - [as Yom Kippur is a day of complete cessation from work].
Rashi: continues - [whoever does not fast or who performs labor on Yom Kippur] is liable to karet - [the punishment of being cut off from the people].
Rashi: continues - [the Mishna concludes by stating the consequences] - [these are the laws of Yom Kippur as described in the Torah].
Rashi: continues - [the High Priest's garments must be pure white linen] - [as specified in the Torah for this service].
Rashi: continues - [the High Priest must be careful to perform all the rites exactly] - [in the order they are prescribed].
Rashi: continues - [if the High Priest makes a mistake in the order of service] - [he must correct it immediately].
Rashi: continues - [the service is repeated from that point] - [until the correct order is restored].
Rashi: concludes - [end of the description of the High Priest's service on Yom Kippur].
